mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp and 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months and 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 2% MoM and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and starts to decrease, it signals a potential easing of monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and starts decreasing, but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, but 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months, combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening economy with increased consumer confidence and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE decreases
regime_hint: expansionary demand with labor market tightening
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE decreases, but 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, or if the joint effect of HOUST and UNRATE changes on 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a potential inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which can lead to increased investment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, but 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
